Orange Beach, let’s slow this one ALL the way down….

I know you’re all FEENING for how this ties into the skies, so here we go down the rabbit hole…… 🕳️ 

The case is Benjamin Walborn and Melissa Walborn v. Orange Beach City Board of Education; Orange Beach City Schools; William Randolph Wilkes, in his official and individual capacities; and Mary Catherine Law, in her official and individual capacities.

Federal Court. Southern District of Alabama. Case No. 1:25-cv-00531. 🔎 

And before anybody tries the lazy “Florida kids” talking point, let’s add the context they conveniently leave out….. 

Ben Walborn is a former U.S. Navy pilot.

After the Navy, he went into private life as a pilot.

A pilot for whom?

Just take a guess…...

But, WRONG answers owe me a Bushwacker and a blackened chicken Caesar salad with double protein from Flora-Bama Yacht Club.

So yes, the minor Walborn children lived in Florida.

That was NEVER the scandal. ❌

Based on court documents, the Walborn children were allegedly enrolled through Orange Beach’s own non-resident student policy, and the out-of-state tuition issue was allegedly paid.

They weren’t sneaking in.

They weren’t freeloading.

They were there under the rules that the City of Orange Beach created.

Now, let’s talk about what the case actually alleges….. 👀 

The incident began in July 2024, after Walborn’s child was allegedly targeted in a private student text thread. Based on court documents, Walborn reported the bullying to Superintendent Wilkes on July 30, 2024, and asked that his child be placed in a different homeroom.

Two days later? 

Both children’s Orange Beach school enrollment was allegedly revoked, effective immediately.

Not suspended.

Not investigated through some meaningful process.

REVOKED. 👏🏻 

Like MY lawsuit AND Shane Haugen’s against Orange Beach Police Department and the City, the Walborn lawsuit alleges constitutional violations, including due process, First Amendment retaliation, and equal protection. 

It also includes claims tied to breach of contract, defamation, arbitrary and capricious decision-making, and requests for declaratory and injunctive relief.

And when the Board/District/Randy Wilkes/Mary Catherine Law tried to get the case tossed?

Again, like my case and much to Tony Kennon’s chagrin, they didn’t get ALL of it tossed.

A federal judge allowed major parts of the case to survive, including allegations tied to custom, practice, and policymaker liability.

That matters…… A LOT. 💃🏼 

Because this isn’t just about one family.

It’s whether Orange Beach’s school system had a practice of treating non-resident students differently when “connected locals” complained.

It’s about whether rules were followed.

It’s about whether paid, enrolled students were given process before the school system yanked the rug out from under them.

And it’s about whether Orange Beach can sell “local control” when it wants applause, then pretend nobody knows who controls what when accountability shows up.

So now let’s talk about Tony Kennon’s imaginary “ethical wall” between City Hall and Orange Beach City Schools.

The City Council appoints the school board.

The school board governs the school system.

The superintendent allegedly made the decision.

Orange Beach wants the ribbon cuttings, the branding, the “local control,” the photo ops, and the credit.

But when federal court starts asking questions about policy, power, influence, process, and who gets treated differently?

Suddenly, Tony wants everybody to believe City Hall and Orange Beach City Schools are strangers passing in the Rouses parking lot.

No, sir.

That is not an ethical wall.

That is a GLASS HALLWAY. 🪞 

Everybody can see straight through it.

And, you don’t get to build the hallway, appoint the people walking through it, pose for pictures in front of it, and then pretend you can’t see the fingerprints on the glass when accountability shows up.

The case is pending and the allegations still have to be proven.

But the point is already loud enough:

The “ethical wall” that Tony wants you to believe in is made of GLASS.

And the whole town is about to see who keeps walking through it and putting their fingerprints all over it. 👏🏻

In 1968, some Agent Orange drums came with two stripes.

The second stripe meant Orange II. The war was spraying Orange faster than the Pentagon could buy it, so one company in Kansas City made a substitute, and nearly a million gallons went to Vietnam.

In 1977 the Air Force burned its leftovers at sea. The VA rule names the chemicals, and both of Orange II's are on the list.

The veterans underneath carried theirs home.

Peace Begins With Us! 
The students of V Orange led a meaningful morning assembly in connection with International Day of Peace, reminding us that peace is not only about living without conflict, it is also about caring for the world around us.
Through their thoughtful presentation, students explored how simple actions such as keeping our surroundings clean, respecting nature, reducing waste, saving water, caring for living things, and being considerate towards others can help create a more peaceful and harmonious world. 
Their message was powerful: When we care for our surroundings, we care for one another. When we choose kindness, responsibility, and respect, we help build a culture of peace.
Peace starts with a kind heart, a responsible choice and a caring hand.
